newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia port strike talks postponed.
newsitem.headline: Colombia port strike talks postponed.

text.p: Top-level talks scheduled for Tuesday morning, which were aimed at ending the six-day-old dock workers' strike at Colombia's main Pacific coast port, have been postponed, a labor leader said Monday.

Representatives of the two dockers' unions involved in the stoppage at the port of Buenaventura, SINBRASEMAR and SINTRAMARITIMOS, had been scheduled to meet Labor and Transport Ministry officials, cargo handling operators and ship owners in Bogota at 9 am (1400 GMT).

But Nelso Amaya, regional head of the Unitary Workers' Confederation (CUT), to which SINTRAMARITIMOS is affiliated, said the meeting had been postponed. Efforts were being made to rearrange talks for later in the day in the southwest city of Cali or in Buenaventura.

"The problem is here in Buenaventura and the workers felt that it should be solved here or at the very least in the (provincial capital) Cali, which is within easy traveling distance for a negotiating committee," Amaya said.

The strike, set off by workers' demands for higher pay and social security, sickness and injury benefits, has paralyzed about 160,000 60-kg bags of coffee and more than 27,000 tonnes of bulk and bagged sugar in port.
A port authority spokesman said 12 ships were blocked in port and it is estimated the port is losing about $500,000 per day during the strike.
Amaya said negotiations could begin Tuesday afternoon or may be put off until Wednesday.
